summary: A genuinely mutual NDA under English law, but it restricts disclosure to advisers and Affiliates, assigns feedback to the discloser, adds a mutual indemnity, EUR 75,000 per-breach liquidated damages and a full-indemnity costs clause.

findings.quote: which is designated as confidential or proprietary at the time of transmission or which, by reason of its character, content or the context of its communication, ought reasonably to be understood by a diligent professional operator to possess a confidential character
findings.why: Marked-or-reasonably-confidential definition, applying to either party's information and covering derived notes and analyses.

findings.quote: solely and exclusively in connection with, and to the extent strictly necessary for, the examination, implementation and furtherance of the Permitted Purpose
findings.why: Use is limited to the Permitted Purpose, a named evaluation of a prospective integration and distribution arrangement.
findings.fallback_cited: Purpose limited to a named project, product evaluation or pilot.

findings.quote: to restrict internal access to the Confidential Information strictly and exclusively to those of its own direct, permanent salaried employees
findings.why: Access is limited to permanent salaried employees, excluding officers, directors and contractors.
findings.draft_redline: Disclosure to employees, officers, directors, professional advisers, auditors, insurers and Group members who need to know, with the Receiving Party liable for them.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We would ask that need-to-know disclosure be permitted to officers, directors, advisers, auditors, insurers and Group members, with each party remaining responsible for them.

findings.quote: to not disclose, disseminate or make available the Confidential Information to any external professional advisers, legal counsel, accountants, auditors, insurers, independent contractors, consultants, or corporate Affiliates without the prior written authorisation of the Disclosing Party
findings.why: Disclosure to professional advisers, auditors, insurers and Affiliates requires specific prior consent, so none is permitted by default.
findings.draft_redline: Each Receiving Party may disclose Confidential Information on a need-to-know basis to its employees, officers, directors, professional advisers, auditors, insurers and Affiliates, and shall be liable for their compliance with this Agreement.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We would ask that routine need-to-know disclosure to advisers, auditors, insurers and Group members be permitted without case-by-case consent, with each party liable for its recipients.

findings.quote: to refrain from disassembling, decompiling, decoding, reverse engineering, decrypting
findings.why: Prohibits reverse engineering of software and technical assets.

findings.quote: able to demonstrate conclusively by contemporaneous written documentation
findings.why: The carve-outs are all present, but the evidence standard (conclusively, by contemporaneous written documentation) is stricter than written records or reasonable evidence and narrows them.
findings.draft_redline: The obligations in Clause 3 shall not apply to information which the Receiving Party can show by written records or other reasonable evidence:
findings.note_to_counterparty: We would ask that the evidence standard for the exclusions be written records or reasonable evidence, rather than conclusive contemporaneous documentation.

findings.quote: advise the Disclosing Party in writing as promptly as possible, and in any case prior to making such disclosure, provided that such advance notification is not expressly prohibited by mandatory provisions of public order or criminal procedure
findings.why: Notice is qualified where legally prohibited and the Receiving Party need only use reasonable efforts to obtain confidential treatment; cost allocation and stock exchange or general law requirements are not addressed.
findings.fallback_cited: Notice 'where lawful' and cooperation at the Disclosing Party's cost.

findings.quote: the Receiving Party hereby irrevocably assigns to the Disclosing Party, with full title guarantee, all right, title, interest and worldwide intellectual property rights in and to such improvements, modifications, derivative works, feedback, recommendations and enhancements
findings.why: Improvements, derivatives and feedback are assigned to the other party, so Halyard as recipient would assign its own developments and feedback to Véloce.
findings.draft_redline: Delete Clause 6.3 and state that each Party retains ownership of its own intellectual property, with no licence granted other than use for the Permitted Purpose.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We would ask to delete the assignment of improvements and feedback, as each party should retain its own developments; Clauses 6.1 and 6.2 already protect each party's disclosed IP.

findings.quote: shall remain the sole and exclusive property of the Disclosing Party or its respective licensors
findings.why: Confidential Information and IP stay with the Disclosing Party and the only licence is for the Permitted Purpose (6.2).

findings.quote: furnished on an "as is" and "with all faults" basis
findings.why: Mutual as-is disclaimer with no warranty and no fraud exclusion removed.

findings.quote: within a strict delay of fifteen (15) Business Days
findings.why: 15 Business Days is 5 or more; officer certificate is provided and clause 8.2 excepts backups and legally required copies, which stay confidential.
findings.fallback_cited: Any period of 5 Business Days or more.

findings.quote: Each Party agrees to indemnify, defend and hold harmless the other Party against all direct losses, claims, liabilities, damages and reasonable legal expenses
findings.why: Mutual indemnity for breach of confidentiality; the playbook allows no indemnity.
findings.draft_redline: Delete Clause 9.2; liability for breach is left to general law.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We would ask to remove the indemnity and leave liability for breach to the general law, which already gives each party an effective remedy.

findings.quote: the Receiving Party shall pay to the Disclosing Party, as fixed liquidated damages and by way of stipulated compensation, the sum of €75,000 for each such individual breach
findings.why: Fixed liquidated damages of EUR 75,000 per breach.
findings.draft_redline: Delete Clause 9.3 and replace with: Each Party shall be entitled to seek injunctive and other equitable relief for any actual or threatened breach, and remedies are cumulative.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We would ask to delete the fixed per-breach sum and instead provide for mutual rights to seek injunctive relief, with remedies otherwise cumulative.

findings.quote: initial term of two (2) years, unless terminated earlier by either Party by serving thirty (30) days' prior written notice
findings.why: Two-year term with 30 days' notice to terminate early, as preferred.

findings.quote: survive the expiration or termination of this Agreement for an additional duration of five (5) years
findings.why: Five-year survival is within 2 to 5 years and trade secrets are protected indefinitely only while they remain trade secrets.

findings.quote: governed by, and construed in accordance with, the law of England and Wales
findings.why: English law and exclusive jurisdiction of the English courts (11.2).

findings.quote: Neither Party may assign, transfer, delegate, subcontract or novate any of its rights, benefits, burdens or obligations under this Agreement to any third party
findings.why: Mutual no assignment without prior written consent.

findings.quote: the prevailing Party shall be entitled to recover from the non-prevailing Party all of its legal costs, attorney fees, disbursements and related litigation expenses on a full indemnity basis
findings.why: A loser-pays full-indemnity costs clause is not covered by the playbook and goes beyond the general law on costs, so it cannot be mapped to a rule.
findings.draft_redline: Delete Clause 12.8 so that costs are left to the discretion of the court.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We would ask to delete the costs-shifting clause and leave costs to the court's discretion in any proceedings.
